question: In India, roads are classified in the _____ classes according to their capacity.
solution:
The correct answer is __**six**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The classification of roads in India** is based on the capacity of the road. This means that the number of lanes, width, and design of the road are all taken into account to determine its capacity.
 
• There are **six classes of roads in India**, with Class 1 being the highest capacity and Class 6 being the lowest. Class 1 roads are typically expressways or highways, while Class 6 roads are rural roads or village roads.
 
• The classification of roads is important for planning and development purposes. It helps policymakers to determine where to invest in infrastructure and which roads are in most need of improvement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• In India, the classification of roads is based on the recommendations of the Indian Roads Congress (IRC). The IRC is a professional organization that provides guidance and standards for road development in India.
 
• Class 1 roads are typically expressways or highways that connect major cities and are designed for high-speed traffic. Class 2 roads are also highways but are designed for slightly lower speeds and connect smaller towns and cities.
 
• Class 3 roads are major district roads that connect smaller towns and villages. Class 4 roads are other district roads that connect rural areas. Class 5 roads are village roads that connect individual villages. Class 6 roads are rural roads that provide access to individual homes and farms.
